The night crew and handler pairs, minutes
It started on time, and the kennel attendant led

Attendees were Naomi Mensah, Fatima Osei, and Buddy.

The desk review focused on keeping the intake area calm and clear, because travelers arrive anxious when pet documents are not ready. The senior coordinator reminded everyone to use a warm professional tone, keep answers short, and move any hold-up to the front without delay. The welcome team was told to check carriers, labels, and comfort items before escorting passengers toward boarding, and to watch for signs of stress in each animal.

We also covered handoff discipline at the counter. Staff must confirm paperwork before accepting a crate, then pass the case cleanly to the next handler pair. Any mismatch in names, carrier condition, or route details must be raised at once so the shift does not lose pace. Buddy was used as the example for calm handling, with emphasis on steady voice, slow movement, and no unnecessary crowding.

The group agreed that the Companion Animal Travel Desk should keep the same steady service style across all passenger contact. Naomi Mensah and Fatima Osei were noted as needing clear reassurance and direct updates, especially if any kennel check or boarding step changes. The meeting closed with a reminder that the desk stays urgent, accurate, and welcoming throughout the shift.

The meeting ended cleanly.
